text:
maria: FYI - we're seeing a ~22% usable GPU capacity drop in us-central around 11:05 UTC. Error rates for Xid/DRIVER have spiked across multiple racks. P95 latency for hosted gen requests up ~40%. :rotating_light:

oliver: seeing same. telemetry shows concurrent ECC correctable counts jumping then nodes being auto-drained by the cluster operator. quick snapshot: rack-12 and rack-14 affected.

sarah: any recent kernel/driver changes rolled this morning? I didn't schedule anything in infra. :eyes:

maria: not on our side. infra deploy-bot shows a kubelet restart job 10:50 but that's from a rollout of the node-exporter. nothing touching drivers.

ryan-oncall: attaching cut of dmesg from a flapping node (shortened):
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 13, PID=0, GPU=0: DRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[  124.001234] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00: GPU reported ECC error - correctable count increased
[  124.567890] ENOSPC: nvidia_uvm failed to allocate 0x1000 bytes
```

oliver: Xid 13 + ECC counts -> looks like intermittent card-level faults, possibly thermal or PCI fabric. but multiple nodes across racks? could be a mezzanine switch or power issue.

infra-bot: Automatic remediation: marked 8 nodes unschedulable and triggered drain loop across two AZs.

maria: Can we pause auto-drain? It's making capacity oscillate and evicting customer workload. If we cordon and hold, we can isolate without mass eviction.

lex: we have a quick mitigation plan: 1) pause cluster auto-drain (set operator to standby), 2) cordon the highest-error nodes and run nvml diagnostics, 3) failover serving traffic to us-west for remaining capacity, 4) schedule hardware swap if diagnostics show repeated ECC increments.

sarah: agree. I'm worried about cascading rollbacks - if it's a switch issue we'll keep seeing new nodes fail. Is there recent fabric flapping in telemetry?

oliver: checking tor-switch logs now. there's a BMC alert on rack-12 at 10:58 and power cycle history lines for pmu-3. correlation looks plausible.

ryan-oncall: i've paused the node operator's automatic drains (operator:standby) and notified support to block further automatic evicts.

maria: thanks. runbook step to gather NVML snapshot on cordoned nodes:
```sh
kubectl exec -it node/<node-name> -- nvidia-smi -q | egrep -i "(Product|ECC|FB Memory|Xid)" -A2
```

lex: also grab PCI device diagnostics and `dmesg | tail -n 200` before reboot. If multiple GPUs show increasing correctable ECC counts within minutes that's a hardware replace.

infra-bot: Capacity impact estimate: ~18-25% across us-central for the next 2-3hrs if we keep cordons + hardware swaps. Cost of routing to us-west estimated +$6k/hr for peak traffic.

sarah: Please announce to product/support that some customers on Dedicated in us-central may see throttling. We should offer to failover dedicated reservations to other regions temporarily.

maria: opened a short incident page and added initial notes. Link: https://go/incident/INC-2026-us-central-gpu-wave (internal)

ryan-oncall: quick note — observed Xid 31 on a node as well, which usually indicates driver hang. Let's not rule out a driver regression entirely. Can infra confirm driver package versions across affected nodes?

oliver: affected nodes: driver v515.105 and v515.107 mixed due to staggered upgrade last month. will list exact builds and map to failure times.

maria: if driver mix is true, throttle rolling restarts and standardize to the known-good build (v515.105) on a small canary set before any mass rollback.

lex: ops decision needed: do we 1) hot-swap suspected nodes now (hardware replace), or 2) attempt driver rollback on a canary? Recommend canary rollback + hardware on confirmed repeat ECC.

sarah: canary rollback seems lower blast radius. But coordinate with hw team to pre-stage replacements in case canary fails.

maria: executing canary: picking 2 nodes in rack-14, cordon -> drain -> install v515.105 -> reboot -> run diagnostics. I'll post results in 15m.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance window: infra will apply driver rollback on canary nodes at 11:30 UTC. Maintenance ID mnt-8732.

oliver: extracted a short chart from telemetry: ECC correctables per-node jumped at 11:04 and again at 11:11. The nodes that jumped at 11:04 are the same with BMC power blips. Rack-level correlation looks high.

maria: update 11:42 UTC - canary node 14-03 returned healthy after rollback to v515.105. ECC counts stable, no Xid logs for 20m.

ryan-oncall: good sign. continue canary on two more nodes but keep auto-drain paused. If stable after 1hr, schedule staggered rollbacks for remaining affected zone.

sarah: notify sales/support: short note for customers: "We're investigating GPU hardware issues in us-central; some workloads may be slower. We're performing targeted rollbacks and hardware diagnostics and will update in 60 minutes."

maria: putting a hold on large autoscaling events in us-central until we complete stabilization. Please avoid triggering cluster-wide rebalances.

lex: post-mortem action items (initial):
- correlate BMC power events with ECC spikes per rack
- standardize driver versions across fleet and add canary guardrails
- add operator pause control to runbook to avoid mass evictions
- pre-stage on-call hw swaps for racks with repeated ECC increases
- estimate customer cost exposure and credit plan if impacted

oliver: I'll pull kernel logs and tor-switch power telemetry and attach to the incident page.

maria: thanks team. we'll update INC-2026 in 30 min with next status. :thumbsup:
